paper.title: Self-organized shortcuts in the Argentine ant

headline: Deneubourg/Goss 1989 ant double-bridge (agent-based): 3/3 locked clauses REPRO; asymmetric short-path fraction 0.99 (5/5 seeds >0.8); symmetric symmetry-breaking 5/5 (winners short/long 2/3)

verdicts.gate: P1 asymmetric (Ll=2Ls): short-path traffic fraction > 0.8 at steady state in >= 80% of seeds
P2 symmetric (Ll=Ls): symmetry breaks — one path wins (final > 0.8 or < 0.2) in >= 80% of seeds, winner seed-dependent
P3 self-reinforcement: cross-seed mean short fraction non-decreasing over the run (tol 0.05) and final >= 0.8

extra.scope: faithful reproduction of a published synthetic/biological model; no real-world data; the contribution is whether the harness + discipline reproduce the self-organized shorter-path selection and symmetry breaking, and would catch an artifact

citations: Goss, S., Aron, S., Deneubourg, J.-L. & Pasteels, J.-M. (1989). Self-organized shortcuts in the Argentine ant. Naturwissenschaften 76:579-581. doi:10.1007/BF00462870.
Deneubourg, J.-L., Aron, S., Goss, S. & Pasteels, J.-M. (1990). The self-organizing exploratory pattern of the Argentine ant. Journal of Insect Behavior 3:159-168. doi:10.1007/BF01417909.

benchmark.note: no cross-tool baseline; faithful single-implementation reproduction graded against the short-path traffic fraction
